JOURNEY TO THE MOON

Chapter 3 · Lunar orbit

The last day of the coast, the Moon growing in the window beside you. Behind the Moon, out of touch with the Earth, the main engine slows you into orbit; coming round, the Earth rises. Two orbits over the Taurus-Littrow valley, a second burn behind the Moon, and a pass at 15 km over where you will land. Sit down in a chair before you start.

In the headset: A or X runs time faster (×10, ×100, ×1000, ×10,000; round the burns, Earthrise and the low pass ×10 at most), Y the big window to your left, hold B to look from outside, right stick press to sit right again. The spacecraft never turns faster than you can comfortably watch: at high speed it holds still while the Moon turns below.

On this screen: drag to look, Space start or pause, W faster, C window, O outside, 1–7 jump.
